title: Dashboard overview with KPI row and table
description: An operational overview screen: a short row of 3-5 KPIs that each show value, unit, comparison period, and direction; one primary chart for the trend that matters most; and a sortable table of the items that need action. The period selector and filters sit in one toolbar that scopes everything below it.
intent: Let a returning user see what changed since last time and jump to the rows that need action, within one screen.
characteristics: 3-5 KPI tiles with value, delta, and comparison period stated in words
one primary chart, not a wall of equal charts
action table below the fold line with sorting and row links
single scope toolbar (period, segment) for the whole page
interaction: Changing the period or segment updates KPIs, chart, and table together and is reflected in the URL. KPI tiles link to the filtered table. Loading keeps layout stable with skeletons.
responsive: KPIs wrap to two columns, then one; the chart keeps a minimum height; the table becomes horizontally scrollable inside its own region with the first column sticky, never the page.
accessibility: KPI deltas state direction in text ("up 4% vs last week"), not color alone; the chart has a text summary or data table alternative; the table uses th with scope and aria-sort.
limitations: Needs real metrics with defined comparison periods; invented numbers are worse than an empty state.
More than five KPIs dilutes the row; split into a second view instead.
